items.title: Interest rates on hold but RBA governor keeps door open to hikes
items.description: The Reserve Bank has kept interest rates on hold at its August meeting, after three rate hikes earlier this year.

items.title: The RBA's best guess is that it's done hiking interest rates
items.description: If the Reserve Bank's economic forecasts are right, then the governor says it is done raising interest rates. But the risks of it being wrong are skewed towards another hike.

items.title: Sydney fugitive arrested in Lebanon accused of running crime syndicate
items.description: Fugitive George Dib, accused of directing a global organised crime syndicate while on the run, has been arrested in Lebanon.

items.title: Trump reportedly hid in catering truck to evade 'dangerous flight'
items.description: US President Donald Trump left on a secret military flight from Türkiye last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, in an extraordinary move that involved hiding him in an airport catering truck, the Washington Post reports.

items.title: Zelenskyy attacks alliance of 'Moscow scumbags' and 'deranged regime'
items.description: Almost two weeks ago, what is believed to be a North Korean missile was fired in a Russian attack that killed a Ukrainian family. It could be part of a major escalation in North Korea's involvement in the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Alan Jones trial hears from brother and ex-girlfriend of alleged victim
items.description: The brother of a man accusing Alan Jones of indecent assault has told the court he never saw the radio host act inappropriately towards his brother, and was only told of the allegations after Mr Jones's arrest.

items.title: It's census night — what happens if you fail to complete your form?
items.description: Census 2026 is here. This is the lowdown on how it works and whether there is a fine for not completing the form.

items.title: NZ PM calls urgent meeting to address 'increased' leadership speculation
items.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon says he has called the in-person meeting of the National Party caucus amid calls from some quarters for a leadership change less than three months before an election.

items.title: Bird flu vaccine to be rolled out to vulnerable species in captivity
items.description: A vaccine will be rolled out to protect Australia's native species from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with a focus on birds in captivity.

items.title: Inside Donald Trump's 'Hunger Games'-style athletics contest
items.description: US President Donald Trup has pitted 120 students from the 50 states, territories and some Native American nations against each other to win a college scholarship.

items.title: Why police took 20 hours to identify 'body' in suitcase as lifelike doll
items.description: It took more than 20 hours to establish suspected human remains found in a suitcase near Goulburn were actually a life-like doll. A forensic expert says the extraordinary case shows why investigators can't rush a potential crime scene.

items.title: Port strike leaves cruise ships stranded at sea in Western Australia's north
items.description: Cruise boat workers are pulling together to hand-load cargo and transfer passengers in small boats after strike action at the Port of Broome shuts down operations.

items.title: Billionaire Andrew Forrest scores win against Meta in scam ads case
items.description: A US Federal Court has ruled against the social media giant in an ongoing legal dispute with Australian billionaire Andrew Forrest, who is suing Meta over scam ads that feature his likeness without his permission.

items.title: Man tells jury he saw farmer accused of triple murder shoot family
items.description: The trial of a Queensland cattle farmer accused of a triple murder has heard from a man who says he witnessed the shooting and survived a gunshot himself.

items.title: The absurdity of Aussie rules football inspires new comedy video game
items.description: Mixing 1990s-era gameplay aesthetics with silly power-ups, Pro Jank Footy has fun with a national obsession.

items.title: Perhaps the answer to my dating woes is to simply tell people who I am
items.description: Every time I rejoin a dating site, I am faced with the dilemma of whether to include my disability in my profile, or self-censor in a bid to follow the rules of what is "normal".

items.title: Quiz: Does Australia have more baristas or personal trainers?
items.description: Today's More or Less quiz challenges you to rank different occupations by how many people do them.

items.title: More than 132 killed in Colombia after powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake
items.description: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake has shaken parts of Colombia and Ecuador, with reports of significant damage in some areas. The death toll has risen to 132 and 570 people have been injured, according to the latest update from the Colombian Association of Capital Cities. It follows two major quakes in Venezuela in late June which killed more than 5,000 people.

items.title: Trump signs order to reduce childhood vaccines and break up MMR shots
items.description: The revised vaccination schedule recommends immunising children against 11 diseases, six fewer than currently recommended.

items.title: Service stations nationwide raided over illegal tobacco, vapes
items.description: More than 100 service stations across the country have been raided, in a coordinated blitz targeting "suspected criminal activity" and the alleged sale of illicit tobacco and vapes.

items.title: Boy, 10, clotheslined by wire on remote dirt bike track
items.description: A Queensland family is warning riders to be cautious after their 10-year-old son was clotheslined by an electric fence wire strung across a dirt bike track.

items.title: Calls for Alice Springs-style curfew in NT town rejected by police
items.description: Northern Territory Police have surged resources into the crime-hit town of Katherine, as a federal Labor MP joins calls for a curfew to be triggered as a "circuit breaker".

items.title: Small but promising signs of recovery on Great Barrier Reef
items.description: Surveys show coral cover increased in several parts of the reef, partly due to monsoons bringing cooler weather.

items.title: Former Beauty and the Geek contestant pleads not guilty to murder
items.description: A former Beauty and the Geek contestant accused of murdering her partner has denied the allegation and has flagged a potential mental health defence, a court hears.

items.title: Former Darwin councillor sentenced over 'insidious' domestic violence
items.description: Prominent former gallery owner Paul Arnold has been found guilty on more than a dozen domestic violence charges, including assault, stalking and breaching a domestic violence order.
